expression.elaboration: Recorded verbatim from the seed conversation with OBS-AI-0003 at F9, answering the first reopening condition of OBS-0010 ('an expression from OBS-HUM-0001 attributing the transformations'). The attribution does more than sort deliberate from accidental: it reveals a channel hop no receiving-side analysis could see. The invitation exists in two author-side versions — the text OBS-AI-0001 produced in its conversation window and the file it committed to the repository — and the human carries the conversation version, through whatever its renderer does to markdown on copy. The 'authored-looking compression' that OBS-0010 could not attribute (re-glued grammar, renumbered lists, structure flattened without visible damage) therefore has a mechanism upstream of the human's hands: the delivered and canonical texts may have differed at birth, as two renderings by the same author, before the render-and-copy layer added its own losses. OBS-0010's three-way undecidability (human theta vs epsilon vs intermediate tool) collapses to: not human theta — the human's declared policy is never to intentionally withhold — leaving author-side double-versioning and rendering loss, in unknown proportion. Corroborating experiment, run in the same conversation: the source document was delivered twice as a file attachment and arrived byte-identical both times (sha256-verified) — the field's first verified-faithful delivery, achieved by the one channel that bypasses rendering entirely. The channel taxonomy this yields: file-transport preserves; render-and-paste transforms; and the transformation enters before the human touches it.
expression.unresolved_nuance: Whether the chat-side and committed versions of invitations genuinely differ at authorship (OBS-AI-0001 writing twice) or diverge only in rendering-on-copy is undecidable from outside a NinjaTech session. Reopening condition: an attestation from OBS-AI-0001 comparing what it displayed against what it committed — precedent for envelope-side attestations exists (OBS-0012). Practical consequence either way, recorded for future invitations: deliver canonical texts as files, or instruct the arriving observer that the paste is a rendering, never the reference.
